what_this_measures: Whether the layers vlm-controls-v4 renders come back identical when the geometry half of that pipeline is repeated in one process. The published visible-pixel fraction moves in its fourth decimal between runs and the question is where that enters.
why_a_set_difference_and_not_a_hash: A cloud written in a different order has different bytes and identical content, and coincident points resolved differently by a z-buffer would be a fair explanation for one pixel. A set difference on exact coordinate triples tells those two apart; a digest cannot.
what_this_establishes: The input to the reconstruction is reproducible and its output is not: fused came back byte-identical across 4 repeats, while retained, subject did not, and not by reordering -- the set differences below are nonzero and the subject's point count itself moves. So the renderer is drawing geometry that genuinely differs, and a pixel count that moves is not evidence about the rasterizer. PR #1024 isolates this reconstruction as the cause of the same class of variation in capability-record-support-crop.json, measured at a fixed thread count and no better at one thread.
what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing about the renderer's own determinism, which is untested here, and nothing new about the cause inside the reconstruction. It also does not revisit the thread count: that lever is already known not to reach this stage, so a repeat under it would measure nothing.

reproducibility.note: Every figure here is a between-run comparison, so the figures themselves are expected to move. The verdicts are what reproduce.
